# Retrospective: PR 12695

## Worked
Read-only security triage and author gating preceded investigation. Fresh Claude Code Opus 5.5 High and Pi Sol Xhigh identities were verified. Independent reports remained unread until both were saved. Source-only review was sufficient for the public scope. Synthetic Git observations were preserved without inflating them into production assurances.

## Corrections and deviations
- Initial coordinator 60-content-line policy reads did not reserve continuation metadata. The reviewer dispatch and all later reads explicitly use at most 50 content lines. Every required policy tail was read.
- Sol registration clearing lagged shell readiness once. Preserve the failed receipt and verify both conditions before launch; this was done without a duplicate launch.
- Opus's fixture guard claim was too broad. Parent-root containment does not individually guard native Git internal writes, interpreter temp files or utilities. Inline substitutions and inner wrapper outputs lacked independent status/stream retention; the server exit check was not an expected-status gate. Preserve the run and original report, accept the audit addendum, exclude broad runtime totals from the public comment.
- Future Git experiments need an explicit native-Git internal-write inventory, not only clone destination guards, and immediate producer gates for every substitution. If individual guards or needed retention cannot be established, prefer source-only conclusions. This correction is recorded in the assignment-local evidence audit and was delivered to the reviewer before closeout.

## Tool observations
No confirmed tooling defect. Herdr's old-agent registration may clear after its shell is ready; readiness polling, not speculative relaunch, is required. The source-subset repository was disclosed accurately as partial and byte-matched to pinned head blobs. The local review tool seal confirms bytes, not semantics or complete safety policy adherence.

## Carry forward
Keep a small, source-supported no-findings comment instead of expanding defense-in-depth, intentional history trade-offs or rare compatibility observations into mandatory findings. Keep all historical evidence, avoid persistent agent-memory edits, and make source-only versus experimental scope explicit.

**Verified by source inspection:** The plugin installer, theme installer and new dev-channel checkout now request `--depth=1`. Existing dev checkouts are reused unchanged. The channel test expectations match the updated clone arguments.

| Clone path | Before | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Plugin / theme installation | Default history depth | Requests depth 1 |
| New dev-channel checkout | Default history depth | Requests depth 1 |
| Existing dev-channel checkout | Reused | Still reused |

The inspected update and version consumers do not require old tags or complete history for ordinary same-branch updates. A new shallow dev checkout also has narrower branch/history visibility, an intentional trade-off rather than an established failure of those consumers.
